source_text:
ταύτην ὁμολογοῦντες τὴν
πίστιν βεβαπτίσμεθα, καὶ οὐκ ἀρνησόμεθα τὸν αἵματι τῷ ἰδίῳ πριάμενον ἡμᾶς

δεσπότην. Οὐκοῦν ὅταν λέγῃ τὸν ἀεὶ ὄντα καὶ ἐξ αὐτοῦ προαιώνιον Υἱὸν γεννῆσαι
σήμερον ὁ Πατήρ, τοῦ σήμερον ἐνεστηκότα καιρὸν σημαίνοντος ἤτοι τὸν τῆς
ἐνανθρωπήσεως, ἐκεῖνο περινοήσωμεν, ὅτι καὶ σάρκα γεγονότα, τουτέστιν
ἄνθρωπον, τὸν ἴδιον υἱὸν διωμολόγηκεν ὁ ςπατήρ, οἰκειοῦται δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ τὴν
δευτέραν αὐτοῦ κατὰ σάρκα γέννησιν. οὐ γὰρ ὅτι γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος, ἀπέστη τοὺ
εἶναι κατὰ φύσιν υἱὸς τοὺ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός, μεμένηκε δὲ καὶ οὕτως υἱὸς καὶ ἐν τοῖς
ἐμφύτοις ἀξιώμασιν, εἰ καὶ πλούσιος ὢν ἐπτώχευσε δι' ἡμᾶς.

Επιτρέπεται η ελεύθερη χρήση του υλικού µε αναφορά στην πηγή προέλευσής του.

1
thought_title: Confessing the faith in which we were baptized
orientation: Cyril is closing his comment on Psalm 2:7, explaining what Christians confess about the Son's eternal being and his birth in the flesh.
pass_a_gloss: Confessing this faith we have been baptized, and we will not deny the Lord who bought us with his own blood. Therefore whenever the Father says that he begot today the Son who always exists and is eternal from him, the 'today' signifying the present time, that is, the time of the incarnation, let us understand that, even when he became flesh, that is, a human being, the Father acknowledged him as his own Son, and he makes his own, as it were, his second birth according to the flesh. For not because he became a human being did he cease to be Son by nature of God the Father, but he remained even so Son also in his inherent dignities, even though being rich he became poor for us.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'Lord' for δεσπότης, referring to Christ as the one who bought believers with his blood.
Glossary requires 'eternal' for προαιώνιος, describing the Son's existence before all ages.
Glossary requires 'incarnation' for ἐνανθρώπησις, the Word's becoming human.
Glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ, the human nature assumed by the Word.
Glossary requires 'Son by nature' for υἱὸς φύσει, distinguishing natural sonship from adoption.
Glossary requires 'faith' for πίστις, the confession received in baptism.

pass_b_english: We have been baptized confessing this faith, and we will not deny the Lord who bought us with his own blood. So when the Father says that he begets today the Son who always exists and is eternal from him—since “today” marks the present moment, that is, the moment of the incarnation—let us understand this: the Father has acknowledged his own Son even when he became flesh, that is, a human being, and he makes his second birth according to the flesh his own as well. For he did not cease to be Son by nature of God the Father because he became a human being. He remained Son even so, and remained in his inherent dignities, even though he was rich and became poor for our sake.
notes: The source has 'ὁ ςπατήρ' with a stray sigma before πατήρ; this is likely OCR damage for 'ὁ Πατήρ' (the Father).
The source has 'τοὺ εἶναι' and 'τοὺ Θεοῦ' with τοὺ for τοῦ; this is likely OCR damage for the genitive article τοῦ.

last_rejected.quote: the Father has acknowledged his own Son even when he became flesh
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν ἴδιον υἱὸν διωμολόγηκεν ὁ πατήρ
last_rejected.why: Greek aorist indicates completed action 'acknowledged,' not pluperfect 'has acknowledged'; changes temporal sense.
last_rejected.fix: the Father acknowledged his own Son when he became flesh
last_rejected.ruling: διωμολόγηκεν is perfect tense, not aorist; 'has acknowledged' is correct. Reported grammatical claim is wrong.

last_rejected.quote: he makes his second birth according to the flesh his own as well
last_rejected.source_quote: οἰκειοῦται δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ τὴν δευτέραν αὐτοῦ κατὰ σάρκα γέννησιν
last_rejected.why: Subject is the Father, not 'he' (the Son); 'makes his own' obscures that the Father claims/appropriates the Son's fleshly birth.
last_rejected.fix: the Father claims as his own the second birth of him according to the flesh as well
last_rejected.ruling: Subject ambiguity of οἰκειοῦται is inherent; 'he' can refer to Father from prior clause. 'Makes his own' is valid for οἰκειοῦται.

last_rejected.quote: he did not cease to be Son by nature of God the Father
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀπέστη τοῦ εἶναι κατὰ φύσιν υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός
last_rejected.why: Greek ἀπέστη means 'departed from/abandoned,' not 'cease'; and 'Son by nature of God' misreads genitive as possessive rather than predicate.
last_rejected.fix: he did not depart from being Son by nature of God the Father
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπέστη + infinitive naturally means 'ceased to be'; 'Son by nature of God the Father' is standard patristic phrasing, not misleading.

problems.quote: So when the Father says that he begets today
problems.why: Pronoun 'he' before 'begets' ambiguous: Father or Son?
problems.fix: Clarify subject: 'when the Father says that he himself begets'.

problems.quote: makes his second birth according to the flesh his own as well
problems.why: 'Makes his own' is vague; likely means 'acknowledges/claims as his own'.
problems.fix: Clarify as 'acknowledges as his own Son'.

edits.old: So when the Father says that he begets today
edits.new: So when the Father says that he himself begets today

edits.old: and he makes his second birth according to the flesh his own as well.
edits.new: and he acknowledges his second birth according to the flesh as his own as well.
